extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating whether an agency's rulemaking complied with the APA §553(b) notice-and-comment requirements and whether courts may require procedures beyond those in the APA. Focused on judicial review of agency procedural adequacy in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA §553(b) notice-and-comment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 553(b) of the Administrative Procedure Act requires that agencies publish notice of proposed rulemaking in the Federal Register, and that interested parties be given an opportunity to participate, or comment, before the agency adopts a final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory baseline for rulemaking procedure — publication of notice and an opportunity for interested parties to comment. The page states this as the procedural requirement agencies must satisfy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy standard: compliance with the text of the APA
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the agency's rulemaking procedures are adequate is measured against the requirements set out in the text of the APA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The case framed the issue as whether agency procedures satisfied APA §553(b). Vermont Yankee held the proper inquiry is whether the agency followed the APA's procedural text; courts should not require procedures beyond that statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on judicially imposed procedures (APA sets 'maximum' procedural requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 553(b) imposes the maximum procedural requirements which Congress was willing to have courts impose upon agencies in rulemaking procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts generally may not impose additional procedural requirements on agencies beyond those specified in the APA. If the agency has complied with the APA's requirements, a reviewing court should not demand extra procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion to grant additional procedural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are free to grant additional procedural rights in the exercise of their discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may voluntarily provide more process than the APA requires (for example, additional notice, hearings, or opportunities to participate). But granting extra procedures is the agency's choice, not something a court can compel absent statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for inadequate proceedings: remand and reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency proceedings are inadequate, courts can remand the agency decision and overturn actions based on deficient procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factual history on the page notes that inadequate proceedings can lead to remand/overturning of agency action (though Vermont Yankee reversed a Court of Appeals remand where the agency had met APA requirements). This describes the practical consequence when procedural requirements are not met.
